newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks set to enjoy year-end rally next week.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks set to enjoy year-end rally next week.

text.p: UK shares have regained their footing and look likely to enjoy the traditional end of year rally next week, providing a volatile Wall Street doesn't spoil the party, analysts said on Friday.
The FTSE-100 index pierced the all-time record high in early trade and then again later with the help of a surge in the Dow.
With technicals indicators pointing higher, the nervous UK share market seems to have finally shrugged off the fall-out from "Frantic Friday."
But analysts said the bull run would be short-lived and would likely peter out early next year as worries of a further UK interest rate rise and fears of an overbought market return to centre-stage.
Chris Chaitow, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities, said the market would likely rally to the end of the year, and cited an ultimate target of 4,200 by early January.
"After that it might get tough," he said. "We'll wait and see what happens in the first few weeks of January but next year stands the risk of being a bad year."
The FTSE 100 settled 26.3 points higher at 4,027.6, but well off the record peak set earlier at 4,100.
Yet technical analysts said a close above 4,073.1 was key for the index, and set it in good stead for the holiday period.
A dearth of economic data and company news in the coming Christmas week may make for a sleepy market, analysts said.
The London Stock Exchange closes at 1230 GMT on December 24 and re-opens for a half day on December 27.
The only UK data due are trade figures for November and October, which are unlikely to contribute much to the on-going interest rate debate in the UK, economists said.
On the other side of the Atlantic, U.S. personal income and spending data for November, and durable goods orders are due next week.
